newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent climbs sharply on expected Iraqi delays.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent climbs sharply on expected Iraqi delays.

text.p: IPE oil futures made sharp climbs in late afternoon trade, buoyed by expected delays to Iraqi exports under the second term of the United Nations oil-for-food deal, and news of Iraqi interference with U.N. helicopters.
July Brent was 35 cents up at $17.85 off a session high of $17.88 a barrel. June gas oil closed 75 cents up at $162.25 a tonne.
Brokers said that bullish news was giving some traders the jitters.
"The selling is exhausted and there's panic to cover shorts with these fairly bullisg stories," said one broker.
Traders said reports that Iraq's ambassador to the United Nations said on Wednesday that there would be no Iraqi shipments in June helped push the market higher.

The second term of the $2-billion oil-for-food agreement was renewed from June 8, but traders have reported delays in signing contracts. Time is needed to put into place a new plan for the distribution of aid and to submit a new pricing formula.

In addition, a senior U.N. official has written to the Security Council detailing four incidents of interference with U.N. helicopters in Iraq "in which the lives of the crews...and the aircraft themselves," were endangered.
After seven straight sessions of losses, brokers said that more downside is limited.
"Open interest has been rising in a falling market...there are a lot of shorts out there which don't want to be exposed if we push up to $18.00," a broker said.
